A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TTT research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v2 reports original language-model evaluations on the Pile and Books3, component ablations, context-length analyses, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original Pile and Books3 evaluations, ablations, and runtime results in the main text and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The TTT-Linear and TTT-MLP architectures, reconstruction objective, learned projections and initialization, mini-batch updates, and primal/dual procedures are retained. Appendix A corrects the mathematical account of the existing procedure without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate language modeling on the Pile at 2k and 8k context and Books3 across 1k–32k context. v3's lead figure switches to an already-covered Pile setting; the newly cited object-recognition work does not add an experiment to this paper.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain Transformer, Mamba, Transformer finetuning, and the linear-attention ablation comparisons. DeltaNet, Mamba 2, and Gated DeltaNet receive related-work discussion without newly reported baseline evaluations. The inconsistent Transformer label in v3 Figure 2 does not establish an actual comparator change.

E3.justification: v3 removes the throughput evaluation and its procedure of doubling batch size until GPU memory is exhausted, then selecting maximum throughput (v2 Section 3.3 and Footnote 15). The stated training configurations and retained latency benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2's analysis selecting context length through minimum perplexity or a Transformer convex hull, summarized in Figure 13, is removed. The underlying Books results and context-length sensitivity plots remain in v3 Figures 15–16. Mini-batch-size, backbone, component, and layerwise TTT-loss analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Section 3.2 states that the TTT experiments were performed in one training run; v3 omits that statement. Neither version supplies seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. This is a loss of run information, without evidence that the number of runs changed.

E6.justification: Under the retained stated settings, prefill timings at 8k change from approximately 19.2 to 13.7 microseconds/token for TTT-Linear and 34.1 to 25.6 for TTT-MLP (v2 Figure 15; v3 Figure 12). Throughput results disappear. Most perplexity results remain unchanged, but v3 Figure 2's 'Transformer' series matches TTT-Linear (T) in the retained Pile-8k comparison in Figure 10, creating an inconsistent reported comparison.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 corrects backpropagation by evaluating the activation derivative at Z^k and multiplying it elementwise by the incoming gradient; v2 instead applies the derivative to the gradient. The dual forward equations also gain the initial-weight subscript. The main equivalence theorems and Appendix B derivation are retained.

C1.justification: v3 recasts the contribution from a new class of layers with broad performance and practicality claims to a framework for instantiating neural networks as hidden states. It removes the abstract's blanket baseline-matching claims and explicit speed claim, replaces the numbered contribution summary, and acknowledges prior linear-hidden-state methods. The long-context utilization claim remains.

C2.justification: v3 expands the existing memory/I/O caveat into explicit uncertainty about whether more expressive instantiations can justify their wall-clock costs. Section 3.2 also explains why MLP capacity helps in long context but can be redundant under matched FLOPs in short context. Most backbone interpretations and future-work limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 removes the identification of ThunderKittens for the forward kernel and Triton for the generation kernel, and omits the explicit training/evaluation context-matching explanation. The training configuration table and JAX/PyTorch access links remain unchanged. The Transformer inference-FLOP disclosure moves from a figure caption to Appendix C.

R1.justification: The modern-RNN and fast-weight positioning is substantially revised around DeltaNet's relationship to TTT-Linear, parallel delta-rule updates, and Mamba 2. v3 adds the earlier TTT manuscript and other relevant references, removes several state-space/fast-weight citations, and drops the claimed uniqueness of the expressiveness–efficiency tradeoff. Its new Gated DeltaNet mentions nevertheless point to the bibliography's GLA entry.

P1.justification: Edits concentrate on the abstract, introduction, experimental discussion, and related work. The numbered contributions become a contributions-and-limitations paragraph, modern RNNs move after the fast-weight discussion, and the runtime account is shortened. Most method exposition and the overall section and appendix structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is recomposed with a Pile comparison and the former Figure 14 token-position plot. The Books context-selection figure and throughput panels are removed, duplicate introductory displays are reduced, and latency axes and legends change. Most diagrams, tables, ablation plots, and appendix result grids retain their presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 improves attribution and claim calibration through its DeltaNet discussion and clearer limitations, and corrects the Appendix A chain rule. However, it introduces a misleading lead comparison: Figure 2 labels the retained TTT-Linear (T) results as Transformer. It also removes throughput evidence and reproducibility details while changing prefill timings without explaining the revision. These benefits and reporting harms prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
